transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-15 10:00 PT; Duration: ~45m; Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marta Silva (Helix Head of ML), Rahul Desai (Helix Cloud Eng), Amir Khan (Helix Security), Sophie Lee (Product)

Summary: quick check-in on onboarding, access, and environment readiness; review of first-pass benchmark numbers; talk about tuning (batching/quantization) and finalize next steps for private/VPC pilot.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we wanted to do a quick weekly sync on the pilot, make sure access is unblocked and go over the benchmark summary priya posted.
[00:12] Marta: hey thanks, yeah excited to be here, we've been trying to get dev infra ready, ran into a couple of service account issues.
[00:20] Rahul: yeah quick note on that, the service account creation ran into the org policy, I removed the temp deny but will need the right IAM roles from you jordon, can you re-send detailed roles?
[00:34] Jordan: absolutely, I'll send the roles matrix after this call, and the onboarding checklist link is in the notes, https://app.redwood.ai/poc-onboarding (note: auto-generated link).
[00:45] Priya: hi all, I'll jump into the numbers quick, first-run latency numbers we saw on the hosted run were median 210ms per token for the 2k prompt using the curated model, when we ran a dev VPC private replica the median moved to 270ms, tail to about 620ms in our short run - there was some cold start on the KV cache.
[01:05] Sophie: just to clarify, is the 270 number with GPU dedciated or shared? (sic)
[01:10] Priya: that's on a small dedicated pool we spun up in the dev VPC, so yes dedicated but constrained to two GPUs for now. We saw better throughput when we enabled batching (batch size 8) but latency per request increases a bit; tradeoff column is latency vs cost.
[01:28] Marta: makes sense. Our SLO is 300ms median for customer-facing features, so 270 is OK but tail is concerning.
[01:35] Priya: yep, tail comes from a few things - cold KV cache misses, occasional node swapping and model quantization artifacts. For the next run I recommend pinning the model to the quantized int8 profile that we validated and enabling prefix cache warmup. That should knock 100-150ms off tail in many cases.
[01:52] Amir: security question - we need to confirm KMS/HSM integration and whether keys are customer-managed. Also SOC2 and audit logs, we have a list.
[02:03] Jordan: understood, we have docs: SOC2 attestation and the audit log export options, I'll share those. For KMS we support customer-managed keys (CMK) in Redwood Private; need the ARN and we can wire it up, we'll include steps in the checklist.
[02:20] Rahul: VLAN/VPC peering - I put the peering request in last night but haven't finished routing. We also need to confirm egress controls for the test nodes.
[02:30] Priya: note, for benchmarking in a private VPC we recommend a test harness that emulates your seq length distribution; if you can share a few sample prompts we'll run the 8k token scenario next, that will stress the KV cache and show mem pressure.
[02:45] Marta: we'll share the prompt set, do you want them anonymized?
[02:48] Priya: anonymized is fine, just preserve length distribution and token patterns.
[03:00] Jordan: quick unplanned topic - competitor callouts, Marta mentioned you evaluated Anthropic and OpenAI earlier; any blockers that specifically pushed you to Redwood?
[03:10] Marta: mainly price predictability and ability to run in our VPC. Anthropic had good quality but their enterprise model was still early for our stack, OpenAI was fine but cost and data residency were questions.
[03:22] Sophie: also support for on-prem eventually is a requirement for us, which you flagged as Redwood Private.
[03:30] Priya: on the tuning side, small checklist: try int8 quant, tune batch size, enable prefix/KV caching, and re-run the 8k token scenario; also consider model size reduction for latency sensitive routes.
[03:45] Rahul: about the KMS details, do you need HSM-level attestation or will CMK with IAM suffice for the pilot?
[03:52] Amir: for pilot CMK is fine, for production we'll want HSM.
[03:56] Jordan: that's typical, we'll document the difference.
[04:05] Priya: one more infra note - we saw some transcription issues in the first logs, likely from our logging agent; when you run the benchmark please ensure the node exporter and logging agent are on the test nodes only, not the full cluster, otherwise you get tail noise.
[04:20] Marta: good call.
[04:30] Jordan: let's circle back to access: Rahul, once you create the SA and give the roles I'll invite the Helix CI account to the dev cluster. Also need the KMS ARN and the VPC peering CIDR confirmed.
[04:44] Rahul: will do, I'll aim to have that by 2026-04-18.
[04:50] Sophie: timeline wise, if benchmarks look good by 4/20 we can start integrating the feature into staging the following week.
[04:59] Priya: yep and if any blockers on security we can schedule a security deep-dive with Amir, Jordan and our security docs team - suggest 60m slot.
[05:12] Amir: yep put me on it.
[05:20] Jordan: recap - Priya will run second benchmark with the 8k prompts, Marta will share prompt set, Rahul will provision service account + KMS + VPC peering info, Amir will send SOC2/ISO Qs. I'll share onboarding checklist and roles matrix and SOC2 docs after the call.
[05:38] Marta: thanks, that's helpful.
[05:45] Jordan: any blockers before we close?
[05:48] Rahul: none from infra, just will need the roles doc which you said you'll send.
[05:55] Sophie: no blockers, thanks.
[06:00] Jordan: great, we'll follow up in email with notes and links. Meeting end.

References / Links shared during call: https://app.redwood.ai/poc-onboarding, security packet link (redwood-sec-package.pdf), benchmark spreadsheet: https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/helix-poc-2026-04-14
